title: Spain says no evidence Morocco orchestrated migrant crisis
gist: A short Al-Monitor podcast episode summary notes Iran launched a new wave of strikes on Kuwait and that Saudi crude oil exports hit a nine-year low, in an episode primarily about Spain finding no evidence Morocco orchestrated a migrant crisis.

themes.theme: Conflict spillover and Gulf oil supply

insights.claim: Iran launched a new wave of strikes on Kuwait, indicating the Iran conflict is spreading beyond direct US/Iran exchanges to hit a third Gulf state.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Strikes on Kuwait would mark a widening of the conflict's geographic footprint to additional Gulf states, raising regional escalation and energy-infrastructure risk beyond Iran and the Strait of Hormuz alone.
insights.quote: Iran launched a new wave of strikes on Kuwait and Saudi crude oil exports hit a nine-year low.

insights.claim: Saudi crude oil exports fell to a nine-year low, the lowest level since roughly 2017, amid the ongoing regional conflict.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A nine-year low in Saudi crude exports is a concrete, trackable data point signaling either demand destruction, voluntary output cuts, or conflict-related shipping disruption in the Gulf — directly relevant to oil-supply and OPEC-market analysis.
insights.quote: Iran launched a new wave of strikes on Kuwait and Saudi crude oil exports hit a nine-year low.
